title: CorvusPay says unauthorized people took user email addresses, IBANs and transaction details
date_note: Dnevno.hr says the unauthorized access was detected on 17 November.
summary: Croatian payment company CorvusPay confirmed, as reported by Dnevno.hr, that unauthorized people accessed part of its information system and took user data and transaction details in its CorvusPayByIBAN service. Dnevno.hr lists email addresses, IBANs and transaction details as taken. The company says card numbers and data needed to authorize payments were not taken, and that it has cut off further access.
plain: A Croatian payment company says outsiders took customers' email addresses, bank account numbers (IBANs) and payment details from its pay-by-bank-account service.
exec: A payment provider says user email addresses, IBANs and transaction details were taken from its pay-by-IBAN service.
action: CorvusPay advises users, as reported by Dnevno.hr, to take extra care with unexpected messages and payment requests and to check suspicious requests directly with the bank or merchant.
geo_basis: country only; the page read gives no city, pinned at Zagreb as the capital

validation.note: Only Dnevno.hr read (relaying the company's confirmation, which it attributes to ICT Business); the company's own notice was not read and no second publisher was found.

review.note: Compared 17 Nov detection, data taken, cards not taken, user advice and single_source status against Dnevno.hr
